correctness.rationale: An arbitrary unordered cut corresponds bijectively to a cyclic outer edge-transition word with even parity, no adjacent ones, and a forced inner-layer word satisfying exact local equations. The length-(2k+2) overlap graph encodes these constraints at every vertex. Exhaustive Tarjan computation over every window for k=4..7 yields no recurrent SCC except the enumerated 1-,2-,5-cycles; all internal degrees equal one. Two-cycle words require n multiple of four for parity, five-cycle words have even transition parity automatically. A separate direct-graph predicate enumeration for every admissible n<=24 matches these counts. The mathematical reduction, state construction, independent direct test and explicit output are included; direct tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The two closest full mathematical records calculate precisely the jump-two and jump-three families, and their fixed-jump theorems do not imply the uniform assertions for k=4,5,6,7. General perfect-matching-cut literature provides recognition and complexity results, not all-order exact counts in these four families. An exact local finite-state reduction supplies new coverage and identifies the rigidity and period-four/five reappearance. Priority is conditional on the accessible and indexed record, and isolated small graph isomorphisms are explicitly excepted as old instances.
residual_risks: The 2014 step-four metric-dimension full article was not available as a complete directly inspected text; only abstract and excerpt were seen, although its predicate is different.

Sporadic graph isomorphisms to earlier fixed-step families cover isolated parameter values, and those finite instances are not new.

value.rationale: The exact four-step all-order classification answers a natural gap after known k=2,3 results and reveals a nonmonotone rigid–resonant sequence: k=4 and k=6 force only the spoke cut, k=5 admits the period-four family, and k=7 admits both period-four and period-five families. This classifies all valid bipartitions into induced two-regular shores joined by a perfect matching, not simply the existence of the universal spoke cut. It is a structural obstruction and complete census for natural fixed families, supported by reproducible automaton certificates rather than arbitrary isolated graph counts.
